question: The introduction of the entry/exit system (EES) was announced several years ago, with the Commission touting it as a tool for improved identity checks at the EU’s external borders. Registering biometric data and digitally recording every external border crossing by thirdcountry nationals are long overdue steps to ensure effective border checks, prevent multiple identities and better combat illegal migration.

However, instead of proceeding decisively, the Commission has repeatedly postponed the system’s introduction. Originally scheduled for 2022, deployment was most recently postponed in December 2024, when the buck was shifted to the Member States.

The delays reveal both an organisational failure in awarding the contract to IT company Atos, formerly led by Commissioner Thierry Breton, which has been less than successful in its implementation, and a lack of political will in tackling illegal mass migration. 1.
What specific challenges have led to the repeated delays to the introduction of the EES, and what steps are being taken to remedy these issues as quickly as possible?

Was an EU-wide procurement procedure held for the contract award, and what steps is the Commission taking so that it does not look as though the award of the contract to Atos, the IT company formerly led by Commissioner Thierry Breton, was a revolving door case?
By what amount have the delays pushed up the originally planned costs?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.6.2025) 1. The start date for the Entry/Exit System (EES) operations has been revised due to several reasons, including disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, technical complexities of the EES design and specific implementation difficulties at central and national levels.

In October 2024, the Justice and Home Affairs Council agreed that a progressive launch of the EES would be the best way forward. Subsequently, the Commission adopted on 4 December 2024 a proposal for a Regulation on a temporary derogation from certain provisions of Regulation (EU) 2017/2226 and Regulation (EU) 2016/399 as regards a progressive start of operations of the EES1.

Co-legislators reached a provisional agreement on the proposal on 19 May 2025. According to the revised interoperability roadmap, endorsed by the Justice and Home Affairs Council on 5 March 2025, the EES entry into operation is foreseen in October 2025. 2.

The EES procurement was carried out by the European Union Agency for the Operational Management of Large-Scale IT systems in the Area of Freedom, Security and Justice (euLISA). The Commission has asked the Agency to provide the information requested by the Honourable Member. 3.

As regards the costs for the development of the EES, the Commission has asked the euLISA to provide the information requested by the Honourable Member. The Commission will send the Agency’s reply to the Honourable Member as soon as possible.
